Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Persistence after transient stimulus (the song that never stops)
ideas.description: Give cells a brief pulse of a stimulus (e.g., TPA, injury, or cytokine) and track AP-1 (FOS/JUN) occupancy and target gene expression by time-course CUT&RUN and RNA-seq for days to weeks after withdrawal. Memory is supported if a subset of AP-1 sites and genes stay in an altered state long after the AP-1 proteins themselves return to baseline.

ideas.title: Priming and re-stimulation challenge (the bird heard in the gale)
ideas.description: Compare naive cells with previously stimulated cells in a second challenge, measuring the speed and amplitude of transcription (nascent RNA, live reporters) at AP-1 targets. Hypersensitive responses specific to AP-1 sites, which disappear when AP-1 is blocked only during priming, would indicate AP-1-dependent memory.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility and pioneer function at memory loci
ideas.description: Run ATAC-seq, histone mark profiling (H3K27ac, H3K4me1) and Micro-C before, during and after stimulation to find enhancers that AP-1 opens and that stay open after the signal is gone. Test whether motif-mutated enhancers (CRISPR) or degron-mediated acute loss of AP-1 (dTAG on JUN/FOS, or dominant-negative A-FOS) block both opening and later maintenance.

ideas.title: Necessity versus maintenance: timed AP-1 degradation
ideas.description: Remove AP-1 acutely at different times (during induction, versus after the memory state is established) using degrons or inducible dominant negatives. If AP-1 is needed only to establish memory, the state persists after loss. If it is also needed to maintain it, the state decays, which separates initiation from true maintenance and from epigenetic carriers like histone marks.

ideas.title: Single-cell and lineage tracking of inheritance through division
ideas.description: Use live-cell AP-1 reporters, lineage barcoding, and paired single-cell multiome (RNA and ATAC) to follow whether the stimulated state passes to daughter cells and in what fraction. Mathematical models can then test whether the persistence is bistable or self-reinforcing, for example a JUN/FOS positive feedback loop, or whether it is better explained by a slowly decaying signal.
